scorecard.title: College Scorecard (location, enrollment, cost; data released 2026-10-15)

cds.title: Clarkson University Common Data Set 2025-2026 (PDF, Institutional Research public reports)

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set 2025-2026 (fall 2025 entering class; some interior page headers still read 2024-2025 but C1 says Fall 2025, C8A says applying for Fall 2027 and G1 asks for 2026-27 costs): 4,948 applied (2,930 men, 2,015 women, 3 unknown), 4,082 admitted, 525 enrolled. The residency rows add up to the totals: in-state 2,312 / 1,965 / 337, out-of-state 1,493 / 1,375 / 153, international 1,143 / 742 / 35 (applied / admitted / enrolled). International (nonresident) first-years are 742 of 4,082 admits. Early decision (C21): 235 applications, 178 admitted. No early action. Waitlist: 44 offered, 9 accepted, 3 admitted. SAT/ACT are optional (C8A: not required, considered if submitted); 49% (251 students) submitted the SAT and 7% (35) the ACT. Average high school GPA printed as 3.732 (95.24% reported; shown as 3.73). Undergraduate enrollment (2,163) is B1 total undergraduates and the nonresident count (143) is the B2 'Total Undergraduates' column. The student-to-faculty ratio (14 to 1) counts graduate students and faculty too.

cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs from the Common Data Set 2025-26 (G1 asks for 2026-27): tuition $61,594 (same for first-years and all undergraduates; $2,053 per credit hour, 12-19 credits), required fees $1,370, on-campus food and housing $19,368 (housing $10,840 + food $8,528). Estimated expenses for residents: books and supplies $1,560, transportation $1,596 and other expenses $900 (other costs shown = transportation + other). No printed total. Clarkson's international tuition page still lists 2024-25 figures ($63,064 tuition and fees plus $19,368 living). CDS H6: 92 degree-seeking nonresident undergraduates received institutional aid, averaging $38,942 (average over need-based and non-need-based awards).
